notes: Entries include guides, descriptions, codes, studies, and project pages; the number of records is not equal to the number of independent trials.
Indexed excerpts and abstracts are clearly separated from the full text.
Some of the research results are described in several related sources.
Version 2.1: qualitative audit of geography; international and cultural applicability; new comparative AI studies 2026. The search is predominantly English, not exhaustive.

Version 2.2: 18 sports sources S80–S97. The previous 79 sources did not undergo a full literature review; original access dates have been preserved. Checked internal links, boundaries and selectively new AI data.
2026-10-08: full package content audit; targeted primary-source rechecks and five additions. Earlier source dates preserved; not 102 independent trials or 102 new full-text reviews.
Public package translated into English in version 0.1.1. Translation does not refresh source check dates or establish efficacy in any language. Runtime answers follow the user’s language.
2026-10-17: Two textbooks were added for bounded background reading; this does not indicate whole-book review or clinical evidence updates.
2026-10-17 cycle009: one selected primary cognitive-training trial and linked supplementary/protocol scope added; counts remain records, not independent replications or full-field appraisal.
2026-10-17 cycle015: selected official social-connection constructs added;112 records are not112 independent trials or full-text appraisals. Original source dates and import pins preserved.

sources.title: Gloster et al. — The empirical status of ACT: a review of meta-analyses
sources.supported: 20 meta-analyses: ACT generally outperforms a range of controls; the exception to the superiority generalization is CBT.
sources.limitations: Read abstract, not full analysis of risk of bias; Overlapping studies are possible.
sources.use: ACT as an informed choice without claiming superiority.

sources.title: NICE NG193 — Chronic primary pain, psychological therapy

sources.limitations: Don’t carry over any pain or all of life’s problems.
sources.use: Example of a recognized ACT indication.

sources.title: ACBS — The Six Core Processes of ACT
sources.supported: Describes the six processes of psychological flexibility, accepting and acting on values.
sources.limitations: Professional organization representing the approach; a description of a model is not independent evidence of a causal mechanism.
sources.use: ACT Terminology; The exercises are written independently.

sources.title: WHO — Doing What Matters in Times of Stress
sources.supported: The official self-help resource, with audio and Russian versions via the page links.

sources.title: WHO — Group Interpersonal Therapy for Depression

sources.limitations: Read the description, not trained on the full manual.
sources.use: IPT in the approach map.

sources.title: WHO — Problem Management Plus, individual psychological help

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF — EQUIP: compendium of competency assessment tools

sources.title: Bradbury and Bodenmann — Interventions for Couples

sources.title: ESSM — Sexual Desire Discrepancy: A Position Statement

sources.limitations: Expert analysis, not a full systematic review and not a validated treatment algorithm.

sources.title: NHS — Low sex drive (loss of libido)
sources.supported: Possible relationships, stress, health, medications and other reasons; If there is concern, an assessment is needed.
sources.limitations: Reference information, not a diagnosis of the cause in a specific person.
sources.use: Don't reduce sexual issues to psychology or hormones.

sources.title: Sharifipour et al. — Impact of CBT on sexual dysfunction of women in reproductive age

sources.title: Green et al. — Psychological treatments for sexual concerns in peri/postmenopausal women

sources.use: A counterargument to a universal sex therapy recommendation.

sources.title: Shoshani et al. — Kai conversational AI trial

sources.use: Active comparisons already exist; consider human crisis support.

sources.population: 185 randomized; 147 eligible participants completed baseline; English-speaking adults; 3-week study of GPT-4o-based ChatGPT and ChatMind.

sources.comparison: External and internal focus; training and competitive pressure
sources.supported: External focus was more useful than internal focus; in the competition phase, both groups improved.
sources.limitations: Small sample, simulator and newcomers; not professional drivers. HRV is not a stand-alone diagnosis of overload.
sources.use: Try out a familiar external landmark with an instructor; do not demand complete calm.

sources.title: Lappi — The Racer’s Mind: How Core Perceptual-Cognitive Expertise Is Reflected in Deliberate Practice Procedures in Professional Motorsport
sources.population: Motorsports Educational Literature Corpus; not a test of athletes
sources.comparison: Qualitative analysis of training procedures and tasks
sources.supported: Motorsports skill involves perception, planning, guidance, feedback and systematic practice.
sources.limitations: A review of trainers' texts does not establish the causal effectiveness of each procedure.
sources.use: Formulate a specific learning task with a trainer and video.

sources.title: McKnight, Manwaring, Felton — Formula 1 drivers demonstrate superior concentration and confidence compared to Formula 2 drivers
sources.population: 10 male drivers: five F1, five F2
sources.outcomes: Self-report of psychological skills; no intervention and no speed measurement
sources.supported: There are isolated differences in attention/confidence; the overall score was not significantly different.
sources.limitations: Small sample, multiple comparisons, elite selection, and lack of causal design. Results are not a recipe for success.
sources.use: Preliminary question card, without an ideal driver profile.

sources.title: Gröpel, Mesagno — Choking interventions in sports
sources.comparison: Interventions against performance deterioration under pressure
sources.supported: A distinction is made between distraction and excessive self-control; Routines and getting used to pressure are addressed.
sources.limitations: Not every error is a choking. The full publisher text was not accessed; the quality of individual designs is uneven.
sources.use: Check the mechanism and train pressure without physical risk.

sources.title: Zeng et al. — Counteracting choking under pressure in sport: A meta-analysis of interventions
sources.comparison: Routines, quiet eye, mindfulness, self-talk and other interventions/controls
sources.outcomes: Accuracy, successful execution, deviation from the goal; open/closed tasks
sources.supported: Positive average effects; for open tasks the result is less robust after adjusting for publication bias.
sources.limitations: Full review not available; real racing is not a test of our cards. Do not transfer quiet eye and hand squeezing mechanically to the controls.
sources.use: Careful pressure rehearsal; take into account the dynamics and unpredictability of the route.

sources.title: Ong, Chua — Effects of psychological interventions on competitive anxiety in sport
sources.population: Various athletes; 34 studies after removing outliers
sources.supported: Supports the ability to reduce competitive anxiety.
sources.limitations: The full text was not accessed. The anxiety outcome is not equal to the outcome of the race; not a universal requirement to calm down.
sources.use: Evaluate both the experience and the actual performance separately.

sources.title: Walsh et al. — Sleep and the athlete: narrative review and 2021 expert consensus recommendations
sources.population: Athletes; age and individual requirements are taken into account
sources.comparison: Expert review, more than one test
sources.outcomes: Sleep, disruption factors, recovery and performance
sources.supported: Travel, early starts and competitions affect sleep; the approach requires individuality.
sources.limitations: The full text was not accessed. Consensus does not establish a universal tolerance for the number of hours.
sources.use: Prepare logistics and bedtime; Do not compensate for fatigue with a psychological ritual.

sources.title: IOC — Mental health in elite athletes: International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026)
sources.population: Elite athletes; not amateur autoslalom and not AI
sources.supported: Help should be taken into account along with the training/competition conditions; sometimes participation requires change.
sources.limitations: Didn't read the entire 48-page document. Not an automatic algorithm for diagnostics or racing clearance.
sources.use: Separate mental performance, clinical care and medicine.

sources.title: AASP — Ethical Principles and Standards
sources.supported: Recognize limits of competence; Clearly discuss services and privacy.
sources.limitations: The Code does not qualify AI and does not replace the law of a specific country.
sources.use: Guide to assistant behavior and relationships with the team.

sources.title: AASP — Become Certified
sources.published: current page; publication date not specified
sources.supported: The CMPC status itself does not designate a person as a sport psychologist.
sources.limitations: Not a reference to the legislation of Serbia or other unknown jurisdiction.
sources.use: Separately check athletic training and clinical qualifications.

sources.title: FIA — Medical guidelines to support driver health and wellbeing
sources.population: Drivers of different levels of motorsport
sources.supported: The driver's medical assessment takes into account the specific requirements of motorsport.
sources.limitations: I read the announcement, not the entire document and not the requirements of a specific series. There is no reason to issue a clearance.
sources.use: Refer medical questions to the relevant team and check current regulations.

sources.title: FIA — New Concussion Awareness Campaign
sources.outcomes: Recognizing a possible concussion; medical assessment
sources.supported: If you have symptoms after the incident, contact your medical team; do not continue if in doubt without evaluation.
sources.limitations: The diagnosis and return period are not set by the chatbot. Check Appendix L/ASN requirements for a specific request.
sources.use: Do not psychologize symptoms after an impact and do not suppress protective fear.

sources.title: AASP — How to identify the right provider
sources.published: the date is not indicated in the document
sources.comparison: Mental performance and mental health services
sources.supported: Mental state and athletic performance may be at odds; The assistant's qualifications depend on the task.
sources.limitations: The Professional Services Scheme is not a diagnostic scale and does not cover unknown jurisdictions.
sources.use: Do not consider a high result as evidence of well-being and do not replace treatment with coaching.

sources.title: Andersson et al. — Efficacy of metacognitive interventions for psychiatric disorders
sources.supported: MCT and MCTraining are separately analysed; MCT has a positive comparative estimate against other cognitive behavioural therapies.
sources.limitations: Abstract read; full methods and indication-specific comparative estimates not independently appraised. Incomplete quality reporting noted by authors. Not a universal ranking or AI trial.
sources.use: Update the earlier single-trial account; distinguish Wells MCT from Moritz MCTraining.

sources.title: Torabi et al. — The effect of metacognitive therapy on depressive symptoms from a transdiagnostic perspective
sources.supported: Positive conclusion for depressive symptoms, with mixed study designs and important uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Uncontrolled studies, severe heterogeneity, publication-bias concerns and internally inconsistent quality/discussion wording. Do not equate pooled control comparisons with universal active-treatment superiority.
sources.use: Document supporting evidence and its limitations rather than adopting the abstract conclusion alone.

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF EQUIP — remote platform
sources.supported: Platform supports trainers and supervisors in assessing and developing helping skills.
sources.limitations: No instrument administration or formal training completed. Human competency instruments do not validate this AI.
sources.use: Inform observable helping-competency criteria.

sources.title: NICE CG31 — OCD and body dysmorphic disorder: recommendations
sources.supported: CBT including ERP; mental rituals and neutralisation; training and supervision requirements.
sources.limitations: Direct fetch 403; official indexed sections inspected. Not a personalised ERP prescription; guideline version must be rechecked for clinical use. Current source-use policy: this identified NICE work remains bibliographic-only pending matching AI permission, not active clinical grounding. Historical reading/access retained; cycle011 repairs selected CBT27 claims, not the whole legacy corpus.
sources.use: Bibliographic/historical source only under current policy; do not bypass through the identified NCBI-hosted NICE work.

sources.title: Sturt et al. — Neurolinguistic programming: systematic review of health outcomes
sources.supported: Limited quantity and quality of research do not establish NLP as an effective health intervention.
sources.limitations: Old search; full contemporary evidence review not completed. Insufficient evidence is not robust proof of no possible effect.
sources.use: Evidence watchlist without endorsing NLP as established treatment.

sources.title: E. Bruce Goldstein — Cognitive Psychology: Connecting Mind, Research, and Everyday Experience (5th ed.), selected Chapter 1 and 7 sections
sources.supported: Selected sections introduce inference about mental processes from response-time contrasts and relearning, describe limits of introspection, and compare behaviorist and cognitive interpretations of behavior. Selected Chapter7 reading introduces retrieval practice, familiarity versus recall, spacing and task-dependent transfer; it does not establish general cognitive or clinical enhancement.
sources.limitations: Only Chapter 1 sections on printed pp. 5–9 and 10–12 were read (PDF viewer pp. 39–43 and 44–46); title, copyright, text, and relevant figures were checked. This fifth edition is a historical conceptual introduction, not a current methods or diagnostic standard. No blanket permission to reproduce the copyrighted text or figures is inferred. On2026-10-17 also read selected Chapter7 printed197–201(PDF231–235),206–207(PDF240–241); visually checked PDF232,234,241 against text. Named subsections only; full chapter, original experiments and contemporary replications not independently appraised. Source SHA verified before rendering; originals unchanged. No tables, figures, exercises or extended paraphrase reproduced.
sources.use: Background for separating observed behavior from a tentative construct interpretation; not evidence for a diagnosis or treatment. Bounded learning/transfer concepts, cited as psychology:S103.

sources.title: Diez, Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Barr — OpenIntro Statistics (4th ed., screen-reader PDF), selected sections
sources.supported: Selected sections distinguish observational studies from experiments, random sampling from random assignment, and discuss selection bias, non-response, confounding, and basic experimental design. Additional selected inference reading explains confidence-interval interpretation, p-values, decision errors, and statistical versus practical significance. Additional paired-data reading explains pair differences as analysis units, uncertainty and within-pair dependence versus between-pair independence; pre/post causality limits combine with prior design reading. Additional sampling-model reading distinguishes observation/statistic/parameter, sampling-distribution variability, standard error and conditional normal approximation. Cycle013 adds fitted-average/slope/intercept interpretation, model diagnostic context and supported-range/extrapolation distinctions. Additional selected reading distinguishes multiplicity, omnibus and particular-pair inference; pairwise nonrejection does not establish equality.
sources.limitations: Sections 1.2.5, 1.3.1, 1.3.3–1.3.4, and 1.4–1.4.1 were read; screen-reader PDF pp. 20, 24–28, and 36 were checked (its pagination differs from the standard PDF). This introductory text is not a full causal-inference or clinical evidence appraisal. The official licensing page describes most Statistics textbook resources as CC BY-SA 3.0; retain attribution and ShareAlike for adaptations and check file-specific terms before redistribution. No source text, figures, tables, or exercises are reproduced here. On2026-10-17 also read selected screen-reader pp202,207–208,211–213,216–218,223–224; visual checks pp202,207,218,224. These are bounded sections/openings, not the full inference chapters or an equivalence/multiplicity review. Current official license page checked2026-10-17; original factual notes and original synthetic illustrations only, no copied textbook exercises or expressive adaptations. On2026-10-17 additionally read screen-reader pp295-297 and301 (4 selected substantive pages),7.2/7.2.1, selected7.2.2 opening/calculation and7.3/7.3.1 opening, not full sections/chapter. File licence/current terms reviewed; automated acquisition for model training is distinct from bounded reading of the licensed edition. No source dataset/example or inference result reproduced; original invented arithmetic only. Clustering, missing pairs and repeated-measures modelling remain unreviewed. Cycle011 researcher/root read seven additional screen-reader pages190–193,195–196,199, selected5.1.1–5.1.6; root visual192–193. Current licence/terms directly rechecked. Broad textbook independence statements not generalized; no copied source examples/code/exercises. Survey, clustering, resampling and missingness methods remain unappraised. Cycle013 researcher directly read8.2.3/8.2.5 on356/360; root independently read/visually checked356/360 and additionally8.2.6 on361. Three distinct substantive pages, not five; page357practice/8.2.7opening not adopted. Current exact-file identity and resource licence/terms checked. Introductory near-normality wording is not generalized to every fitting method. No source quotation/example/figure/exercise/code/data reproduced; prediction intervals, robust/clustered/time-series inference and clinical model validation remain separate study. Additional 2026-10-17 section 7.5.6 reading: printed/PDF329-331, three distinct new pages; researcher and integrating reviewer both read them and visually checked330. Introductory ANOVA/pairwise account only; not a general method for dependent benchmarks, adaptive selection, false-discovery analysis or clinical trials. Source examples/formulas/figures/exercises are not reproduced. Exact-file identity and current license/terms checked.
sources.use: General study-design background; cite as psychology:S104 when referenced across namespaces.

sources.title: Judith S. Beck: Cognitive Behavior Therapy, Basics and Beyond, third edition
sources.supported: Selected assessment, individualized goals/fit, progress/feedback and treatment-plan revision concepts.
sources.limitations: Researcher read printed71-73,160-163,365-367 (viewer90-92,179-182,384-386); root title/copyright/contents and visual viewer179. Not whole chapters/book; clinician training text, not comparative efficacy or AI protocol. Original work year unverified. Publisher terms/permissions inspected, no AI-specific restriction found; source expression/cases/dialogues/forms excluded.
sources.use: Bounded clinical-practice concepts, with current evidence separately appraised.

sources.title: A-Tjak et al.: One year follow-up of ACT and CBT for adult depression
sources.supported: Defined adult depression trial/followup comparing ACT and CBT; nonsignificant differences do not establish equivalence.
sources.limitations: One82person trial;2021 report is follow-up, not independent replication. Substantial missing follow-up observations and selected population; mediation does not by itself establish unique causal mechanism. CC BY4 article-specific notice checked; source tables/instrument rules not copied.
sources.use: Bounded comparator/outcome/application example; no universal equivalence or personal treatment choice.

sources.title: Nordahl et al.: MCT versus CBT for adult generalized anxiety disorder
sources.supported: Selected GAD sample/protocol comparison favourable to MCT on worry/recovery; not universal superiority.
sources.limitations: Small three-arm sample (CBT28,MCT32,waitlist21), predominantly self-report outcomes, substantially mistimed CBT one-year assessments; that collection/publication was abandoned in favour of two-year follow-up; training/protocol and setting matter. CC BY4 article-specific licence checked; no scale items/scoring copied. Cycle009 current selected publisher/licence recheck confirmed the existing URL and DOI10.1192/bjo.2018.54; this does not rewrite earlier reading actors or imply a complete correction audit.
sources.use: Condition/protocol-specific active-comparator interpretation, not a complete comparative evidence map.

sources.title: Hardy et al.: Enhancing Cognitive Abilities with Comprehensive Training
sources.supported: Comparison-specific untrained-test transfer, with unresolved missing-endpoint and meaningful-outcome inference limits.
sources.limitations: Selected main methods/outcomes/discussion, S1 additional-analysis prose and protocol1,3-4; root visual protocol1,3,4. Article-specific CC BY4 and current PLOS accompanying-material terms checked. No dataset reanalysis, source tasks/tables or scales redistributed; no complete harms/missingness/registration-history or systematic cognitive-training review. Source note and exact actors/scopes: docs/goal-study-cycle-009-review.md.
sources.use: Preserve a positive measured comparison without inferring objective everyday function, durability or every-product efficacy.

sources.title: Yang and Wang: self-talk and attentional control under noise distraction
sources.supported: Defined laboratory comparison and task-outcome/transfer limits; motivational group had more antisaccade errors.
sources.limitations: Researcher narrative Study1/2 methods/results/discussion; root selected Study1 and Study2 recruitment/design/procedure/analysis/results/discussion/limits. CC BY4 article-specific notice and PLOS terms checked. Abstract/discussion instructional-benefit discrepancy and inconsistent noise/error discussion retained; no established superiority to silent control.39 analyzed male athletes, post-recruitment exclusions and no competition/retention/harms appraisal. Numerical tables, datasets, peer review and replication not appraised.
sources.use: Bounded sport-psychology evidence appraisal, not training prescription or universal benefit/harm.

sources.title: NIMH: Psychotherapies
sources.supported: Different therapy purposes and elements, problem-specific fit, professional training and progress questions.
sources.limitations: Root read overview/elements/therapist questions and NIMH copyright/third-party/no-endorsement rules. Educational overview, not comparative efficacy or validation of project practices. Images, provider directories and crisis numbers not imported.
sources.use: Independent scope/fit grounding for general CBT educational map.

sources.title: NIMH: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, unwanted thoughts and repetitive behaviors
sources.supported: Compulsions may include mental actions; CBT/ERP educational explanation, initial anxiety/dropout and professional assessment context.
sources.limitations: Root read selected signs, diagnosis and psychotherapy sections, identity and specific reuse notice. NIMH text is public domain unless otherwise indicated; images excluded, attribution/no endorsement retained. No ritual/neutralization protocol, drug dose, efficacy comparison or individual plan inferred.
sources.use: Independent bounded OCD/ERP explanation; full protocol and specialist review remain separate.

sources.title: Office of the U.S. Surgeon General: Social Connection advisory, selected constructs and limitations
sources.supported: Distinct subjective experience, network structure, support function and relationship quality; optional editorial clarification is separately identified.
sources.limitations: Researcher/root selected printed6–7,10,opening12,selected67–68 and69–70 notices. Official synthesis with English/expert-led selection, not full systematic review, primary efficacy study or validated dialogue. Current HHS disclaimer inspected; no explicit matching AI restriction found in that scope. Ordinary copyright/nonfederal editing is not an automatic processing ban; no all-report public-domain or broad licence claim. Figures/stock images/source expression/cited works excluded. Root native download403; no visual pixels inspected.
sources.use: General adult construct explanation in SOC-C1; no disease-risk estimate, minimum-contact prescription, absent-person diagnosis or intervention benefit.

sources.title: Maxim Dorofeev - Jedi Techniques (Russian edition, 2017)
sources.supported: Author proposals for capture, actionable wording, reviews, useful intermediate results and work intervals; not efficacy evidence.
sources.limitations: Complete 2017 FB2 reading by the authorized collaborating reviewer: all 1597 canonical events, appendices, 92 bibliography entries, 88 endnotes and 79 image assets; source body-text preservation and asset identity checked. The integrating reviewer separately read EPUB sections 2.2, 3.2-3.4.2, 3.6-3.6.3, 3.7.3, 4.1.4 and 7.17. Shared attribution is not independent duplicate whole-book reading; full FB2 coverage is not automatically claimed for another format. External bibliography works not implicitly appraised. Section locators, no fixed print/PDF equivalence. Copyright retained; no source text, examples, tables or checklists redistributed. Publisher page is bibliographic, not proof of the exact current edition.
sources.use: Optional original task-support adaptations; metaphors and anecdotes are not clinical or mechanistic validation.

sources.title: Maxim Dorofeev - The Jedi's Path: Finding Your Own Productivity Method (Russian third edition, 2021)
sources.published: 2021; corrected and expanded third edition; Mann, Ivanov and Ferber; ISBN 978-5-00169-383-3
sources.supported: Author proposals for optional observation, small practices, capacity-sensitive plans, purpose and workload selection. Further author proposals treat task wording as both a practice and an indicator, permit incremental list maintenance, and describe small multi-component trials rather than this project one-change simplification. Full reading also distinguishes processing incoming material, accepting a request and completing an action; a permanently empty inbox is not required.
sources.limitations: Complete collaborative EPUB reading: integrating reviewer through 6.4.13, authorized collaborator 6.5 and concluding material, including all 155 endnotes and 106 bibliography entries. All 28 spine members, 155 text chunks and 173 image assets covered with attributed notes; source body-text sequence and asset hashes checked. Some tiny pale handwriting in figure 46 could not be confidently transcribed; its structure and surrounding explanation were read. Shared coverage is not two independent full readings. External research, audio and links not implicitly appraised. EPUB section locators, no fixed-page equivalence. Copyright retained; no copied examples/forms/figures. Current publisher link points to a later supplemented edition, not proof of equivalence to the read 2021 text. Testimonials, clinical claims and maturity levels are not validated outcomes, recommendations or scales.
sources.use: Optional task-support adaptations; reject compulsory tracking and clinical claims from author models.

sources.title: Sam J. Gilbert - Strategic offloading of delayed intentions into the external environment
sources.supported: Four online experiments report improved delayed-intention performance with reminders; bounded memory-aid rationale.
sources.limitations: Full methods, supplements and replications not appraised. PMC direct fetch initially challenged. UCL record identifies CC BY 3.0; no source text/tasks/figures reproduced. Not a test of Dorofeev, this assistant, distress treatment or general daily functioning. Complete correction/retraction audit not performed.
sources.use: Separate reminder-task performance from broad productivity and clinical outcomes.

sources.title: Masicampo and Baumeister - Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals
sources.supported: Specific plans reduced goal-related cognitive interference in described studies; emotion changes were not necessary.
sources.limitations: Abstract through indexed primary record; direct page incomplete and alternative format unavailable. Full methods, bias and replications not appraised; complete correction/retraction audit not performed. APA copyright retained, no full text redistributed. Not evidence that planning treats anxiety or validates an entire task system.
sources.use: Keep cognitive interference distinct from emotional relief and clinical benefit.

sources.title: Vohs et al. - A Multisite Preregistered Paradigmatic Test of the Ego-Depletion Effect
sources.supported: Confirmatory analyses did not establish the hypothesized depletion effect; exploratory analyses differed.
sources.limitations: Selected abstract, participants/protocols and discussion, not full supplements or reanalysis. 36 laboratories; substantial preregistered exclusions. Not proof that fatigue is unreal, and not a direct test of the books. Copyright retained; no source instruments, tables or extended passages reproduced. Complete correction/retraction audit not performed.
sources.use: Prevent literal resource-tank explanations while preserving uncertainty.
